newsitem.title: USA: NY gasoline imports seen undermining spot diffs.
newsitem.headline: NY gasoline imports seen undermining spot diffs.

text.p: New York Harbor spot gasoline traders say differentials are likely to come under downward pressure next week amid expected arrivals of above-normal volumes of gasoline and blendstocks imports from Europe.

"There's a lot of juice coming in. We're going to be inundated by stuff from Europe within the next five days," one East Coast trader said," noting that over 90 percent of U.S. gasoline imports arrive in New York Harbor (NYH).
He said buyers have yet to be found for several 500,000 barrel cargoes of conventional unleaded and reformulated gasoline expected to reach New York Harbor by November 29.
But other traders, while acknowledging imports were on a definite upswing, were not predicting a dramatically steep incline.
"It's more than ordinary because a lot of cargoes will be hitting at once, but it's not a flood," one player said.

"A lot of it is Russian low-octane stuff. And some is European G-TBB," one trader said, referring to lower-quality "To Be Blended" gasoline that is upgraded with MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether), butane and other additives that enable the imported fuel to meet federal specifications.

Differentials on U.S. Gulf Coast conventional unleaded have slipped about five cents a gallon since Nov 14, losing steam as downed catalytic crackers returned to service at Petroleos de Venezuela SA's PdVSA Amuay refinery in Venezuela and the Sun Co Inc refinery in Marcus Hook, Pennsylvania.
Imports expected in the next week include:
* A 500,000-barrel Conoco cargo from Emmingham, England expected by November 29.
* A 315,000-barrel Statoil cargo from Bilbao, Spain, expected by November 25.
* A 338,000-barrel Mobil Corp cargo from Yanbu, Saudi Arabia, expected by November 25.
* A 270,000-barrel British Petroleum cargo from the Mediterraean.
* A 280,000 barrel British Petroleum cargo from Western France expected by November 28.
* A 280,000-barrel Nova Corp. cargo from Northern Spain due by November 25.
* A 325,000 barrel Total cargo expected by November 27.
